governance.note: neiso-57 = the 2026-07-09-neiso-56-reserve-coopt keeper recipe (byte-identical run_config, CLI flags, winter fuel-security stack, reliability drag, temp_dependent_derate, energy_reserve_coopt) with ONE structural addition: neiso_dynamic_reserve_requirements=True — the in-LP co-opt families' static published requirements (NEISO_RCPF_PRODUCTS 1,800/1,200/600 MW) replaced by the MEASURED as-enforced hourly reserve-requirement series from ISO-NE's public ISO Express 'Hourly Reserve Requirements' report (ancillary-hourly-rr; the reserve-requirements clean datatype; system ROS row), the exact NEISO analogue of the NYISO issue-#1344 measured-requirement channel. A measured market-design INPUT (rule 13: regenerates forward as published-static-base + ISO-NE's published condition rules on forward states; responds to changed conditions); measured reserve PRICES stay validation-only and are never read; ORDC shortfall steps stay anchored to the published static shape and translate with the hourly requirement; zero parameters fitted to any residual. PROBE registered per rule 15; NOT promoted. Result recorded honestly: the mechanism ENGAGES for the first time on NEISO — the measured system 30-min requirement exceeds the static 1,800 MW in all 26,280 train hours (mean ~2,300 MW) and on the scored P2 pass the 2025-06-24 18:00 heat-wave hour goes reserve-short at the measured 2,909 MW requirement, stacking a $125/MWh RCPF into the LMP (system max $397, the model's first >$300 train-year hour; that hour IS one of the 12 actual DA>$300 hours, DA $418). Everywhere else the ample fleet still clears the measured requirement free (reserve dual $0.00 in 26,279 of 26,280 P1 hours; P2 identical except the one hour). C3c 2025 remains short of gate (model 1h vs DA 12h); C5b 2025 storage discharge unchanged (0.827 vs actual 2.08 TWh). SEASONAL CORRECTION to the ledger: the actual DA>$300 tail is winter-driven only in 2023 (all 5 hours Feb 3-4 cold snap); 2024's 5 hours and 11 of 2025's 12 hours are SUMMER heat-wave evening peaks (2025: Jun 24 x5, Jul 16 x3, Jul 29 x3, Dec 8 x1) — the C3c gap is seasonal peak-load scarcity-price formation, not a winter-only phenomenon. Zero-forcing twin binds the same event deeper (2h, dual to $250, max $531): the winter-fuel/reliability floors keep capacity generating at low output that also carries reserve headroom, so forcing OFF makes the system reserve-shorter — the floors act as the analogue of the real market's reliability commitments.

exceptions.reason: FIRST tail-hour formation on NEISO: the 2025-06-24 18:00 heat-wave hour binds the measured 30-min requirement (2,909 MW) and stacks a $125/MWh RCPF into the LMP — that hour is one of the actual DA>$300 hours (DA $418). The remaining 11 actual hours (Jun 24 x4 more, Jul 16 x3, Jul 29 x3, Dec 8 x1) still clear reserve-free: the LP's summer supply (perfect availability at derated nameplate, cost-based offers) overstates real headroom at seasonal peaks. Seasonal attribution of this ledger item REVISED: predominantly summer peak-load scarcity in 2024/2025, winter only in 2023. Remaining admissible direction: the ERCOT G-22 analogue — scarcity-anticipating DA offer formation at healthy reserves from measured ISO-NE DA energy offers conditioned on a forward-reproducible tightness driver (charter Limb B); never an offer adder tuned to the tail.

exceptions.magnitude: model 0.827 vs actual 2.08 TWh (-60.2%; unchanged vs neiso-56/neiso-55)
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (downstream of the price_tail / winter-scarcity item)
exceptions.reason: PS arbitrage throughput tracks the intraday price spread. neiso-57 tested the measured-requirement channel: the co-opt now binds exactly one 2025 hour, far too brief to move Northfield/Bear Swamp cycling — discharge unchanged (0.827 TWh). The under-cycle is spread-compression plus unremunerated reserve/regulation cycling; may only move DOWNSTREAM of price structure (never via a storage knob). With the 2025 actual tail now attributed predominantly to SUMMER peaks, the missing winter spread and the missing tail are partially distinct gaps; the remaining admissible closure path for both is charter Limb B (measured DA offer formation).

exceptions.metric: C2 gas family grid-delivered TWh (preliminary 2025 vintage)
exceptions.magnitude: +2.6% vs corrected EIA-930 grid gas (commercial band)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (EIA-930 gas-vs-OTHER fold-in + preliminary-vintage incompleteness)
exceptions.reason: 2025 is a preliminary EIA-923 vintage - per-class actuals are incomplete (13/30 prior CC_REGULAR plants missing, 57% reporting). The scorer falls back to the EIA-930 grid gas cell, which includes geothermal+biomass; the correction formula under-corrects because the preliminary vintage's per-class cells are incomplete. Same categorization issue as the complete-vintage years, where the per-class C1 gate PASSES under the load-scaled band. NOT closable by adjusting model dispatch. Unchanged by temp_dependent_derate.

exceptions.metric: C1 coal + steam-gas winter-energy under-run (within the C1 band, non-gating; documentation)
exceptions.magnitude: COAL_BIT model ~0.06/0.11/0.23 vs actual 0.18/0.24/0.27 TWh (2023/24/25); ST_GAS similar
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (structural; same winter fuel-security family as price_tail and storage)
exceptions.reason: The energy-only LP runs coal/steam only at the temperature-floor commitment plus the hours delivered gas is dear enough; the real units ran more on winter fuel-security / local-reliability commitments. Closable only via the documented winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build, never by cranking the floor slope/cap or an offer adder. Within the C1 band, non-gating. Unchanged by temp_dependent_derate.
